Tag: Allow spaces, ignore case and cap at 5
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags must be a single alphanumeric word and are compared
case-sensitively, so "Resident Fellow" cannot be a tag and "RA" and
"ra" are treated as different tags. A contact can have any number of
tags, and they are shown alphabetically rather than in the order they
were added.

RAs categorize contacts with multi-word labels, and a card cluttered
with duplicate or excess tags is slower to scan during an incident.

Let's
* allow letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, up to 50 characters, and
  collapse extra spaces
* compare tags ignoring case and display them with the first letter
  of each word capitalized, keeping acronyms such as "RA" intact
* limit each contact to 5 tags, in add, edit and the data file
* report a specific error for an empty, too long or invalid tag
* keep tags in insertion order on the contact card

The rules live in Tag, Person and ParserUtil so that add, edit and the
upcoming tag command share one definition of a valid tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to tag a contact by name
commitResults.messageBody:
There is no way to add a single tag to an existing contact. The only
option is edit, which needs the contact's index and replaces all of
their tags.

An RA on duty wants to categorize a contact quickly, without first
looking up their index or retyping their existing tags.

Let's add "CONTACT_NAME /tag TAG", which adds one tag to the contact
with that full name, ignoring case and extra spaces. It reports an
error if the contact is not found, already has the tag or has reached
the 5-tag limit.

The input has no command word, so AddressBookParser only treats it as
a tag command when the first word is not a known command word. This
keeps every existing command working as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Tidy code, tests and docs
commitResults.messageBody:
A review of the tag command against the project's code quality, style
and testing guidelines finds a few gaps. The parser and StringUtil use
unnamed string literals, a wrapped lambda is indented 4 spaces instead
of 8, and tests repeat the same tag setup in several classes. The UG
section is much longer than other commands', and the DG lacks a
diagram for the feature.

Let's
* name the regex group and whitespace literals
* fix the wrapped lambda indent in AddressBookParserTest
* share the max-length tags and a 4-tag contact as test fixtures, and
  test a very long contact name
* trim the UG section and the DG manual tests to the essentials, and
  note that the tag command's parameters cannot be reordered
* add a sequence diagram for the tag command to the DG

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tag filter to list command
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command always shows every contact and ignores any text after
it, so there is no way to see only the contacts with a given tag.

An RA on duty often needs one group at a glance, such as all residents
or all hall staff, rather than scanning the full list.

Let's add "list /filter TAG", which shows only contacts with that tag,
ignoring case and extra spaces. Any value is a valid filter; one that
no contact has shows an empty list with a message instead of an error.

Any other text after list is now rejected, so a mistyped filter such
as "list /filtr RA" fails instead of silently showing everyone.

The /filter parsing lives in TagFilterParser so that other output
commands, such as find, can support it by calling the same method.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix test compilation errors from merge
commitResults.messageBody:
The test sources do not compile. A merge dropped the closing brace and
@Test annotation between two tests in ListCommandTest, and a test in
AddressBookParserTest calls parseCommand without declaring the checked
ParseException.

No test can run until the test sources compile.

Let's restore the missing brace and annotation, and declare the

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command: Accept tags and remove tag command
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags are added with a separate command typed as CONTACT_NAME /tag TAG.
It is the only command without a command word, so AddressBookParser
needs a special case to recognize it, and it adds only one tag at a
time.

Every command should start with a command word, and an RA should be
able to set up a new contact fully in one command.

Let's,
* let add take an optional /tag with a comma-separated list of tags
* parse add with ArgumentTokenizer, so /phone and /tag can be given in
  either order and a repeated keyword is rejected
* remove TagCommand, TagCommandParser and the special case in
  AddressBookParser
* update the UG and DG to match

Commas are used as the separator because they are short to type and
cannot appear in a tag name. Tags on an existing contact can only be
changed with edit for now, which replaces all of them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Person: Remove methods for adding a single tag
commitResults.messageBody:
Person has hasTag, isTagLimitReached and withAddedTag, which were used
only by the removed tag command. Nothing in the app calls them now.

Unused methods add to what readers must understand and maintain.

Let's remove them, along with their tests and the KAI test person that
only those tests used.

A future command that edits tags can restore them from history if its
design needs them.

commitResults.messageTitle: PersonTest: Test that tags keep their given order
commitResults.messageBody:
No test checks that a person's tags keep the order they were given in.
The only test that did was removed with withAddedTag.

Contact cards show tags in this order, so a change that breaks it
should fail a test.

Let's add a test that creates a person with tags out of alphabetical
order and checks that getTags returns them in that order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command parser: Tidy up tag parsing and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommandParser#parseTagList takes an Optional parameter, and
AddCommandParserTest builds the same invalid format message in three
tests.

Optional is meant for return values rather than parameters, and the
repeated message is duplicated test code.

Let's make parseTagList take the /tag value as a String, leaving parse
to decide whether /tag was given, and extract the repeated message into
a constant.

AddCommandParserTest does not test a tag at the maximum length, tags
with valid hyphens and digits, a repeated tag at the tag limit, or
empty arguments.

Without these, a change could reject valid tags or count repeated tags
towards the limit without any test failing.

Let's add tests for each of these cases.
Checkstyle fails CI on the unused assertInstanceOf import.

The team's master adds optional rooms to add, while this branch moves
tagging into add and removes the tag command. Both rewrote how add
parses tags.

Let's keep the room field and validation from master and this branch's
tag model, with these choices for tags:

* Tags are given by repeating /tag, one per tag, instead of a
  comma-separated list.
* A repeated tag is rejected rather than merged.
* /phone, /room and /tag may follow the name in any order.

The UG, DG and tests are updated to match.

commitResults.messageBody:
Tests build persons with a room by copying every field into a new

limits are copied into its test, and some boundaries are untested.

Repeated setup is harder to maintain, and the gaps leave room and tag
edge cases unchecked.

Let's add PersonBuilder#withRoom and use it, include the room in
PersonUtil#getAddCommand, share the parser's length constants, and test
the maximum phone length, a repeated tag at the tag limit and keywords
in the wrong case. Let's also assert that /phone is present after the
format check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Levenshtein distance helper to StringUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
StringUtil has no way to measure how different two strings are.

Fuzzy name search in the find command needs to count how many typos
separate a search word from a name word.

Let's add StringUtil#levenshteinDistance, which returns the minimum
number of single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions
between two strings.

A small hand-written implementation avoids adding a library for a
single method.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find command: match names with typo tolerance
commitResults.messageBody:
find /name only lists contacts whose full name matches exactly,
including case.

An RA on duty often remembers only part of a resident's name, or
mistypes it under pressure, and then finds nobody.

Let's make find /name list contacts whose name words are close to the
search words, ignoring case. Each search word may have more typos the
longer it is, so very short words still have to match exactly.

The matching lives in a new NameFuzzyMatchesPredicate, so delete /name
keeps using the exact NameEqualsPredicate and a typo cannot delete a
different contact.

Fixes #59

commitResults.messageTitle: Move field parsing from PersonField to ParserUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonField parses and validates name, phone, room and tags itself,
then calls ParserUtil for part of the work. Field parsing is split
across two classes, and PersonField grows with every field added.

Let's move the full parsing of each field into ParserUtil, and each
field's length limit and messages into its model class, as Room and
Tag already do. PersonField now only lists the fields and how they
are read and parsed.

ParserUtil#parseTags now rejects repeated tags, matching what add and
edit already did; it had no other callers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Edit command: Let an empty optional field clear it
commitResults.messageBody:
Only repeatable fields can be cleared with an empty prefix, so
"edit 1 /tag" removes all tags but "edit 1 /room" is an error and
there is no way to remove a contact's room.

Let's reset any optional field given with no value to its default,
so one rule covers /room, /tag and fields added later. Required
fields given with no value are still rejected.

RAs keep details such as allergies or how a resident prefers to be
reached in separate chats and documents, so they are not at hand
when the contact is needed during a duty shift.

Let's add an optional note, set with /note in add and edit and shown
on the contact card. It is registered as a PersonField, so add and
edit support it without changes to either parser, and an empty
/note in edit removes it like other optional fields.

Notes are limited to 200 characters to keep the card readable, and
cannot contain "/" because it marks the start of a field. The note
is stored as an optional JSON property, so existing data files still
load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Highlight the note on the contact card
commitResults.messageBody:
The note is shown in the same plain small text as the phone number,
so an RA scanning the list during a duty shift can miss details such
as an allergy.

Let's show the note as an amber callout with dark text, so it stands
out from the gray rows and the blue tags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy code from the note feature
commitResults.messageBody:
The contact card repeats the same show-or-hide steps for room and
note, isValidNote and isValidRoom have Javadoc that does not say what
they return, AddCommandParserTest builds the same person in two
helpers, and the phone length limit is written in three places.

Let's extract the repeated card and test code into helpers, reword
the Javadoc, and build the phone regex and message from MAX_LENGTH.

commitResults.messageTitle: ParserUtil: Share the checks of text field parsers
commitResults.messageBody:
parseName, parsePhone, parseRoom, parseNote and parseTag each repeat
the same three checks: not empty, not too long, and valid. Only the
limit, the validity check and the messages differ.

Let's describe each field's limit, check and messages as TextRules,
and run the checks in one helper. Error messages and the order of
the checks are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java assertions are disabled unless the JVM is started with them
enabled. Tests enable them, but ./gradlew run does not, so a broken
assumption goes unnoticed during manual testing.

Let's enable assertions for the run task, so they fail fast while
the app is being tried out.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note feature: Add defensive checks and logging
commitResults.messageBody:
The note feature's new methods trust their callers: null arguments
fail later with unclear errors, the shared text checks do not state
what they assume about their input, and clearing a field is not
logged.

Let's add requireNonNull checks to the public entry points, assert
the assumptions of private helpers, validate TextRules when it is
created, and log at FINE level when edit clears a field. Note text
is not logged, because it may hold residents' welfare details.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add Room and Note to the Model class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The Model class diagram shows Person with only its name, phone,
email, address and tags, so it no longer matches the code.

Let's add Room and Note. With current versions of PlantUML and
Graphviz the "* all" and "* filtered" labels are drawn next to the
wrong arrows, so let's show the role names in the middle of the
arrows, which keeps them readable however the diagram is rendered.

The help window shows and copies the AB3 user guide URL, which

Users who open help are sent to instructions that do not match
RaContact.

Let's point the help window to RaContact's user guide and update the
